blocks.text: Every summer, at the end of June or the beginning of July, a meadow on the edge of Edirne, near the border with Greece and Bulgaria, fills with wrestlers covered in olive oil. This is Kırkpınar, the best-known tournament of *yağlı güreş*, oil wrestling, and one of the oldest wrestling festivals in the world. In 2010 UNESCO added it to its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Its beginning is told as a legend. In the version given by Turkey's Ministry of Culture and Tourism, the Ottoman prince Süleyman Pasha crossed into the Balkans in 1346 with forty soldiers. Resting near the village of Samona, today in Greece, the men wrestled one another, and two of them, the brothers Ali and Selim, could not beat each other. They wrestled all day and through the night, by the light of candles and torches, until both died of exhaustion. Their friends buried them under a fig tree, and later, the story goes, springs of water were found flowing there. The meadow became Kırkpınar, **forty springs**.

After the Balkan Wars the tournament moved closer to Edirne, and since 1924 it has been held at Sarayiçi, a green island in the river beside the city. The festival lasts a week and keeps its ceremonies. Its patron, the *Kırkpınar ağası*, once sent candles with red bases to towns and villages to invite the wrestlers, a custom still kept as a symbol. On the opening day the golden belt is carried through the city, and forty bands of *davul* (drum) and *zurna* (shawm) players fill the field with music.

Before each bout the *cazgır*, the announcer, presents the wrestlers in verse, with their names, titles and skills, and leads them onto the field with a prayer. An oiler pours olive oil over them, and the pair perform the *peşrev*, a ritual warm-up in which they slap their thighs, clap and hop lightly, before greeting each other. Wrestlers wear only the *kispet*, tight leather trousers from the waist to below the knee, made of water-buffalo or cow hide.

The oil makes every hold slippery, and until 1975 a bout had no time limit and could last for hours. Today the top category has forty minutes, followed by a short scored extra time. The winner is expected to lift his beaten opponent from the ground and console him before the referee announces the result. The champion of the top category becomes *başpehlivan*, chief wrestler, and holds the golden belt for a year; a wrestler who wins three years in a row keeps it for good. Wrestlers learn the sport as apprentices of a master, and UNESCO's description stresses the values expected of them: generosity, honesty and respect for tradition.
Here is Kırkpınar in the Turkish of this unit:

blocks.tr: Kırkpınar'da pehlivanlar zeytinyağıyla güreşir. Yağlı bir pehlivan elinizden kayabilir. Bir güreş kırk dakika sürebilir. Seyirciler bütün gün güreş izleyebilir. Ama herkes başpehlivan olamaz: altın kemeri her yıl sadece bir pehlivan kazanır.
blocks.en: At Kırkpınar the wrestlers wrestle covered in olive oil. An oiled wrestler can slip out of your hands. A bout can last forty minutes. The spectators can watch wrestling all day. But not everyone can become chief wrestler: each year only one wrestler wins the golden belt.

questions.explain: *Kırk* is forty, *pınar* a spring of water.

questions.q: How can a wrestler keep the golden belt for good?
options: by winning three years in a row

sources.title: Kırkpınar oil wrestling festival
sources.note: Inscribed in 2010 on the Representative List; held in Edirne; the Kırkpınar Golden Belt and the title of chief pehlivan; the Kırkpınar Aga as patron; forty bands of davul and zurna; the belt carried through the city; a master of ceremonies who introduces each wrestler in verse; the oil man; kispet of water-buffalo or cow leather; training from master to apprentice; generosity, honesty and respect

sources.title: Kırkpınar Wrestling
sources.note: The legend: Süleyman Paşa and forty soldiers in 1346, the wrestle at Samona (today in Greece), the brothers Ali and Selim wrestling through the night by candle and torch light, buried under a fig tree, the springs and the name Kırkpınar; held at Virantekke after the Balkan Wars and the First World War, and at Sarayiçi in Edirne since 1924

sources.note: No time limit until 1975; since then 40 minutes for the top category, followed by scored extra time; the peşrev
